species.name: Crappie
why: Water 62°F on top, a bit cool for them, so they feed in the warmest water they can find.
Best water today is 18–22 ft deep, mostly on channel edges.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 50 ft, cold below.

species.name: White bass
why: Water 62°F on top, a bit cool for them, so they feed in the warmest water they can find.
Best water today is 18–22 ft deep, mostly on wind-blown banks.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 50 ft, cold below.
South wind at 9 mph pushes bait onto the north shore: try the wind-blown banks.

species.name: Largemouth bass
why: Water 62°F on top, much colder than they like, so they move slowly and stay deep.
Best water today is 16–28 ft deep, mostly on sheltered coves.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 50 ft, cold below.
South wind at 9 mph pushes bait onto the north shore: try the wind-blown banks.
